title: The Man Selling Tools
sceneText:
At midday a man drives a cart up to the estate gate. He is not from around here.

The cart is loaded with tools. Sickles, forks, several ploughshares. The goods do not look bad, and the price is half what it should be.

You call Gregor over to look. He walks once round the cart, picks up a sickle, turns it over to look at the joint where the haft goes in, and scrapes a thumbnail along the edge.

He puts the sickle back, says nothing, and steps back twice to stand behind you.

You notice that none of it is stamped. Ironwork around here is stamped, and the stamp means it is guaranteed.

effects.logEntry: You bought a set of unstamped tools from an outsider.

choices.resultText:
You bought them. Eight guldmark, well over half of what the smith would have cost, and they can be used today.

Gregor helped carry them off the cart without a word. When it was unloaded he went back to the stable.

The tools do work. How long they will hold is another matter, but what you need is this autumn.

effects.logEntry: You sent the man selling tools on his way.

choices.resultText:
You said no.

He did not press you. He has probably been turned down a good many times along the road. He drove the cart off.

Gregor stood beside you and watched it go.

“The edges are good,” he said. “The hafts are new wood. Not seasoned.”

He paused.

“Use them a month, catch one wet spell, and they will want replacing.”

That was the only stretch of speech he made all day.
